interest: Preserves wartime intelligence on Japanese rationing, inflation, and shortages, including a detailed 1943 report on rationing and food cuts.
overview: This file (894.5017) from the U.S. State Department's central decimal files relates to economic conditions, cost of living, price control, and rationing in Japan between October 1942 and November 1944. The documents include cross-reference sheets concerning a British Ministry of Economic Warfare study on European rationing priorities and Japanese deficiencies, a State Department Far Eastern Affairs memorandum, and a detailed despatch from the American Embassy in Chungking enclosing a Chinese intelligence bulletin article by Seisaku Shioni on daily life under Japan's rationing and price control system. The file also contains intelligence telegrams from U.S. missions in Moscow and Bern relaying reports from Japanese, Soviet, and German sources regarding severe cuts in Japanese consumer goods quotas, rising wholesale price indices, and official Nippon Bank cost-of-living increases, concluded by a 1950s departmental charge-out sheet.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting Despatch No. 6123 from Great Britain transmitting a Ministry of Economic Warfare paper on European rationing and Japanese deficiencies.
subfiles.summary: Two cross-reference copies of an October 1942 despatch from Great Britain forwarding a British Ministry of Economic Warfare study, 'European Rationing Priorities and Japanese Deficiencies.'
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 6123 on European Rationing Priorities and Japanese Deficiencies

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum analyzing a report on Japanese price ceilings, rationing, and material shortages.
subfiles.summary: Memo reviews a Chungking despatch: Japan's price situation is less alarming than reported abroad due to strict price ceilings, but raw material and consumer goods shortages will worsen as the war continues.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Division of Far Eastern Affairs on Japanese Price Control and Rationing

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a Chinese intelligence bulletin article on Japanese rationing and commodity shortages.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Gauss transmits and summarizes a China Information Committee article by Seisaku Shioni on Japan's rationing and shortages, calling it credible and predicting Allied bombing will severely disrupt production and distribution.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1741 from Chungking on Price Control and Commodity Shortages in Japan

subfiles.about: Article describing the stringent rationing regulations and living conditions in wartime Japan.
subfiles.summary: Shioni's article details Japan's rationing system: monthly rice rations, matches, soap, and egg shortages, a shift to potatoes and rabbit breeding, a clothing point system, poor synthetic and fish-skin footwear, and warnings of winter food crises and future bombing damage.
subfiles.title: China Information Committee Daily Bulletin Article: 'Japanese People Live Life of Rationing Cards'

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting Soviet newspaper coverage of Japanese press announcements on reduced ration norms.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 500: Harriman reports from Moscow that Soviet papers cited Tokyo Asahi on new April 1944 ration cards cutting Japanese consumer manufactured-goods allowances by 50-60%.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 500 from Moscow on Tokyo Asahi Report of Reduced Ration Norms

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting German press figures for the Japanese wholesale price index in July 1944.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 6645: Harrison in Bern reports Japan's July 1944 wholesale price index at 260.9 (up from 257.4 in June, 247.8 a year earlier), with wheat up to 290.7 and textiles at 345.3.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 6645 from Bern on Japanese Wholesale Price Index

subfiles.about: Telegram relaying Berlin statistical reports on Bank of Japan cost-of-living increases.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 7772: Huddle reports from Bern that the Bank of Japan's cost-of-living index rose 6.3% in the first half of 1944, with cigarettes up 53%.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 7772 from Bern on Nippon Bank Cost of Living Index

subfiles.about: Departmental charge-out sheet recording loans of files between 1952 and 1953.
subfiles.summary: Form DS-933 charge-out record tracking files loaned in 1952-53, including decimal file 894.5018/6 charged out April 15, 1953.
subfiles.title: State Department Form DS-933 Charge-Out Record
